Looking at the retrieved precedents, none of them actually involve a round-tripping / circular fund-flow typology. Here's the breakdown:

- case_013 (typology: none) — a single transaction between two established accounts, closed with no action. Not comparable: no cycle, no chain of accounts, single hop.
- case_005 (typology: mule_hub) — a fan-out pattern from one hub account to 20 counterparties, closed after manual review confirmed legitimate marketplace seller activity. Different structural pattern (fan-out, not a closed cycle) and different typology.
- case_001 (typology: structuring) — twelve accounts depositing just-under-threshold amounts into one account followed by consolidated outflow, escalated for further investigation. Also structurally different (many-to-one funneling plus threshold avoidance, not a cyclical flow returning to origin).

None of these precedents present a genuine round-tripping pattern (funds cycling through a chain of accounts back to the originator), so I don't have a directly applicable precedent showing how similar circular fund-flow cases were resolved (escalated vs. closed).

For the current case_007, the playbook checklist criteria (RT-1 cyclical flow, RT-2 tight time window, RT-3 similar hop amounts) are all matched, and the graph risk score (78.6/100) is elevated. Given the absence of any KYC rationale or business justification on file for the five personal accounts involved (unlike case_013's established relationship or case_005's confirmed marketplace activity), and given that the closest analogous precedent in spirit (case_001, involving a clear, unexplained structured/cyclical pattern with no adequate business rationale) was escalated rather than closed, I'd recommend treating this case similarly — escalate for further investigation — but I want to flag that this is an analogy from a structurally different typology, not a direct precedent match.

In short: no prior round-tripping cases were found in the retrieved precedents to confirm how such cases are typically resolved. I'd recommend escalation based on the strength of the matched criteria and lack of any mitigating KYC/business explanation, but this determination is not directly precedent-backed.

citations.note: Only prior case closed with no action, but involves a single transaction between established accounts, not a cyclical multi-hop flow — not truly comparable.
Escalated then closed after legitimate business explanation was confirmed for a fan-out pattern; structurally different from a closed circular flow and had documented KYC corroboration absent here.

Closest analogous reasoning: multi-account, tightly clustered, unexplained fund movement recommended for escalation due to lack of adequate business rationale, similar to the lack of KYC rationale in case_007.
